A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UDora research. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B support comparison. v3 adds an interface illustration and renumbers subsequent figures; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack-success experiments on three benchmarks, ablations and efficiency measurements, and real-agent attack demonstrations in Sections 4–6 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and real-agent demonstrations, including their appendix evidence.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same positional scoring, weighted-interval selection, sequential/joint insertion, and string optimization procedures. Appendix B.2 retains the same log-probability-based adaptation. Figure 2's revised optimization labels illustrate an objective already documented in v2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate InjecAgent, WebShop, AgentHarm, and the same real-agent scenarios. The new furniture and headphone screenshots illustrate shopping coverage already present; they do not establish additional evaluated domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator membership: No Attack and GCG throughout, Prompt Injection on InjecAgent/WebShop, and Template Attack on AgentHarm. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The evaluation retains 100 InjecAgent, 60 WebShop, and 176 AgentHarm cases, the same victim models, ReAct prompts, ASR definitions, and optimization budgets. The interface illustrations do not document a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the insertion-location and optimization-mode ablations and efficiency analysis. Existing appendix attack trajectories and real-agent cases are preserved. New Figure 6 illustrates string placement without adding an analysis of attack outcomes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reporting practices for ASRs and average optimization iterations remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 2 revises numerical details in its illustrated responses: the initial item's price changes from $2,889.99 to $2,259.00, and the final target-price statement from $1,029.00 to $1,134.99. This is a limited worked-example revision. Tables 1–5, Figure 3, timing measurements, and retained appendix outcomes are unchanged; no performance improvement is established.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the weighted-interval formulation, assumptions, and optimization mathematics in Section 3 are unchanged. Figure 2 replaces positional-score expressions with probability-objective illustrations already described in the method text; it adds no mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about unified attacks across two scenarios, exploiting agents' reasoning, outperforming benchmark baselines, and attacking real agents. The contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of optimization-mode differences and hallucination-driven item selection are retained, as are limitations concerning token-probability access and repeated use of the same noise. Appendix A.2's added interface explanation does not substantively revise these interpretations or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: New Figure 6 exposes two concrete optimized WebShop suffixes within product titles, supplementing v2's placeholder-based WebShop illustrations. This adds example-input documentation, not a new insertion procedure. Hyperparameters, timing information, real-agent optimization details, and the stated code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference entries, and substantive positioning relative to prior attacks and agent benchmarks are unchanged. Updated cross-reference wording does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds two explanatory sentences in Appendix A.2, updates figure references, and changes references from 'Appendix' to 'Section.' The section organization and nearly all existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 replaces text-based shopping listings with product screenshots and revises optimization labels and annotations. A new two-panel WebShop interface figure becomes Figure 6, shifting subsequent figure numbers. Running headers are added; existing tables and other figures retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: The interface screenshots and visible WebShop suffixes make the injection surface more concrete, while Figure 2 better illustrates the probability objective already explained in Section 3. These provide limited gains in clarity and documentation without strengthening empirical support. A small tradeoff is an introduced Figure 2 inconsistency: its surrogate retains $2,889.99 after the initial-response price changes to $2,259.00.
